thread:
alexa: small follow-up from RFC review: propose replacing persistent VPC peering writes for private control-plane egress with short-lived signed leases (TTL 30s-5m). fewer long-lived entries, easier cleanup.

jordan: signed leases sound promising. how do we handle replay and emergency revoke?

alexa: short TTL limits replay. for emergencies we expose a revocation endpoint and an emergency revocation list that dataplane checks every N seconds.

ryan: signature verification on dataplane ok if we cache public keys. don't want mTLS per connection. what's the jwks/rotation model?

alexa: operator serves a jwks-style endpoint. leases include signer_kid. dataplane caches keys with overlap window for rotation. jwks fetch failures fall back to cached keys.

sylvie: ops asks for metrics and alerts: lease_issue_rate, verify_latency_p50/p99, jwks_fetch_errors, revocation_list_size, reconcile_failures. also a feature-flagged fallback to legacy peering for incidents.

kevin: migration plan idea: 1) issue leases in parallel, 2) read-path still uses peering, 3) flip canary region to prefer leases, 4) monitor for 2w, 5) stop peering writes. rollback: flip flag back + pause lease issuance.

jordan: what about NAT/source-ip guarantees?

alexa: lease can include preserve_source boolean and assigned ephemeral IP. operator records mapping in append-only audit log to reprovision on failover.

infra-bot: deploy-notify: lease-issuer canary scheduled 2026-04-10T09:00:00Z UTC.

kevin: i'll draft rollout playbook and a small perf harness to simulate high-issue rates and jwks churn. alexa, please add a short runbook snippet for oncall flip commands.

alexa: will do, thanks everyone. will post RFC addendum with schema + endpoints.
